{"Author":"jFray","Name":"EchoSim","InternalName":"EchoSim.Plugin","AssemblyVersion":"2.0.0.0","Description":"Simulates a full-length fight for your job using your own gear or a best-in-slot preset, then reports the DPS and shows exactly where it came from. Compares gear, melds and consumables, checks your openers and burst windows, and analyses an FFLogs report against the simulated ceiling. Kills on supported encounters can be scored and submitted to per-job leaderboards.","Punchline":"Simulate your rotation, then see how your real kills measure up.","LastUpdate":1793564047,"Changelog":"Added:

The live score has a bar under the number, filled to your score, so it reads at a glance without you having to look straight at it.

You can set how big the live score is drawn - Small, Medium or Large - under Settings, Live Score.

Settings has an About tab, showing your EchoSim, game and Dalamud versions.

The timeline has minute markers, so you can find a point in a long fight without scrolling past every row on the way to it.

The burst chart has axes.

Your profile's older eras can be collapsed.

The leaderboards tell you what happened to your last submitted kill.

Changed:

The interface has been rebuilt. Nine tabs are now four pages - Build, Result, Analyse and Compete - with Settings behind the cog, and the job you are simulating, the Run button, the status line and your DPS sit in a bar along the bottom that is there whichever page you are on.

The window is one fixed size, chosen to fit the pages, and the two size sliders are gone.

The row of job icons is gone. The job you are simulating is a chip at the bottom left - click it to pick another.

Fight length, potion timings and target count are one control each, rather than a slider, a typed box and a row of preset buttons between them.

Settings is four tabs: Appearance, Live Score, About and Changelog.

Appearance offers thirty-one colour schemes in seven groups, including EchoMix's and EchoGlam's own, where there used to be five.

Reporting a bug has moved into Settings, About. It used to be a button in the window's corner.

Live Score is no longer marked beta. What the badge was there to say is said plainly instead: a job's modelled ceiling is corrected whenever a submission shows it is wrong, and every score measured against it moves when it is. That is how it works rather than a phase it is passing through.

The leaderboards now have seasons, and the boards you have been climbing were the beta. It closed on 8 September, when patch 7.56 enabled the Echo in AAC Heavyweight - so those standings are final, and whoever was on a board then keeps that rank and score permanently. Season 1 begins with Evercold.

Scores set since the beta closed are still kept, verified and shown to you on the board and your profile, marked out of season. They are not ranked.

There is one leaderboard per fight holding every job, instead of one per job. A filter on the board puts it back to your job alone, and your title is still awarded on your rank among players of your own job.

Your profile is a list of fights rather than a grid of tiles, so the scores read down one column.

The leaderboards and your profile say what the score is measured against. The number used to sit under a column headed Score with no scale anywhere on the page, which invited reading it as an FFLogs percentile.

Analyse says which of its three steps you are on, and leads with your parse.

Analyse shows one finding at a time with its explanation beside the list. Every finding used to show its whole explanation at once.

Gear Compare's headline percentage is labelled a stat weight estimate. It was presented as expected damage, which is more than that figure can support - it has no rotation and no raid buffs in it, and it can read a set worse than your own gear while winning a real simulation.

Best in Slot simulates both a set that reaches your job's speed tier and one that spends nothing on speed, and keeps whichever does more damage. It used to buy the tier whatever it cost.

Changing page is quicker. It used to hold the page you had just left for a moment before showing the one you asked for.

This changelog is grouped into Added, Changed and Fixed, and the older entries have been rewritten to match. Nothing was dropped from them.

Fixed:

Analyse now names the job on a parse for a job EchoSim does not simulate. It was printing FFLogs' own spelling - DarkKnight - beside a blank icon.

The live score no longer reads "no simulation for this job yet" for a job it does simulate, which it did for the first moments of every pull after you changed job.

The live score panel no longer resizes itself. It grew a line whenever a phase transition paused it, and changed shape again on a job it cannot score.

The live score's hundredths could read 97 for a score of 98.

The live score follows your font scale. It stayed the same pixel size however large the rest of the plugin was.

The window no longer opens larger than your screen, and no longer reopens off the edge of it after you change resolution.

A page that fails no longer takes the rest of the window with it. The other pages, the Run button and the bug report all stay available.

Best in Slot no longer logs warnings about your relic having no substats and your gear having empty sockets while it is part way through building a set.

A Sage record on M3S that a later kill had overwritten is back on the board.","ApplicableVersion":"any","RepoUrl":"https://github.com/jfraygit/EchoXIV/tree/main/EchoSim","Tags":["dps","simulator","rotation","theorycrafting","parse","leaderboard"],"CategoryTags":["Utility","Jobs"],"DalamudApiLevel":15,"IconUrl":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jfraygit/EchoXIV/main/icons/echosim-icon.png","DownloadLinkInstall":"https://github.com/jfraygit/EchoXIV/releases/download/latest/EchoSim-latest.zip","DownloadLinkUpdate":"https://github.com/jfraygit/EchoXIV/releases/download/latest/EchoSim-latest.zip","DownloadLinkTesting":"https://github.com/jfraygit/EchoXIV/releases/download/latest/EchoSim-latest.zip","IsHide":false,"IsTestingExclusive":false,"_SourceId":"echoxiv-com-pluginmaster-json","_SourceName":"EchoXIV","_SourceUrl":"https://echoxiv.com/pluginmaster.json"}

{"Author":"dajoey","Name":"Gluttony Combo","ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"1.0.4.324","CategoryTags":null,"Changelog":"v1.0.4.325 (2026-11-02) [testing]
- **Treasure dungeons: no AoE while the mandragora pack is alive.** The five mandragoras (onion, egg, garlic, tomato, queen) in the treasure dungeons have to die one at a time, in order, for the full reward, and an AoE on the clumped pack breaks the order. While any of them is alive, the auto-rotation runs its single-target rotation only, and any action that can hit more than one enemy is held: cleaves, circles, cones, lines and ground areas (Circle of Scorn, Glare IV, Flare Star, Salted Earth and the like, including damage-and-heal actions such as Assize), plus actions whose follow-up is an AoE (Standard Step and Technical Step, the primal summons and Enkindles, Living Shadow). A held weave is skipped; a held GCD is replaced by the button's current single-target action (Glare IV becomes Glare III, Standard Step becomes Cascade), and readiness checks report held actions as not ready so rotations move on to their next priority. The same applies to single-target buttons pressed by hand. Heals, mitigation (Reprisal included) and party buffs are not held, and an AoE button pressed by hand still does what it says. Normal rotation resumes as soon as the last mandragora is dead. Covers the Hidden and Lost Canals of Uznair, the Shifting Altars of Uznair, both Lyhe Ghiah dungeons, the Excitatron 6000, the Shifting Gymnasion Agonon, Cenote Ja Ja Gural and the Vault Oneiron.
- A dance already in progress when the pack appears cannot finish until the pack is dead, because its finish is an AoE.
- A held GCD with no single-target action on its button waits instead: Red Mage holds Grand Impact, and while Grand Impact is ready the game shows it in place of Jolt III, so that GCD waits until the pack is dead or the buff ends (instant casts, Verstone, Verfire and the melee combo still go; a hand press of that button does nothing meanwhile).
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.324 (2026-11-02) [testing]
- **A pull started by another plugin no longer stalls on the opener's first self-buff.** While a plugin such as Henchman, AutoDuty or Lazy Fate Automation drives the rotation, the out-of-combat restriction already lifted for attacks, but a self-only action with a long cooldown from a damage preset still waited for combat. When the opener's first step was one of those (Machinist's Reassemble or Flamethrower before the first shot), the rotation targeted the enemy and then waited for an action it was never allowed to press, so the character stood at the target until it was pressed by hand. Now, while another plugin is in control and the chosen target is an enemy within 25 yalms, any self-usable action the damage rotation picks fires out of combat as part of the pull: the opener's buffs, and also a heal dump or shield the rotation chooses at that moment. An enemy further away is one the plugin is still travelling to, so buffs are not spent on it early. With no plugin in control, with no enemy targeted, or with the enemy out of reach, the out-of-combat rule is unchanged: heal dumps, shields and other self-only actions from a damage preset still wait for combat.

- **Treasure dungeons: no AoE while the mandragora pack is alive.** The five mandragoras (onion, egg, garlic, tomato, queen) in the treasure dungeons have to die one at a time, in order, for the full reward, and an AoE on the clumped pack breaks the order. While any of them is alive, the auto-rotation runs its single-target rotation only, and any action that can hit more than one enemy is held: cleaves, circles, cones, lines and ground areas (Circle of Scorn, Glare IV, Flare Star, Salted Earth and the like, including damage-and-heal actions such as Assize), plus actions whose follow-up is an AoE (Standard Step and Technical Step, the primal summons and Enkindles, Living Shadow). A held weave is skipped; a held GCD is replaced by the button's current single-target action (Glare IV becomes Glare III, Standard Step becomes Cascade), and readiness checks report held actions as not ready so rotations move on to their next priority. The same applies to single-target buttons pressed by hand. Heals, mitigation (Reprisal included) and party buffs are not held, and an AoE button pressed by hand still does what it says. Normal rotation resumes as soon as the last mandragora is dead. Covers the Hidden and Lost Canals of Uznair, the Shifting Altars of Uznair, both Lyhe Ghiah dungeons, the Excitatron 6000, the Shifting Gymnasion Agonon, Cenote Ja Ja Gural and the Vault Oneiron.

- **A pull started by another plugin no longer stalls on the opener's first self-buff.** While a plugin such as Henchman, AutoDuty or Lazy Fate Automation drives the rotation, the out-of-combat restriction already lifted for attacks, but a self-only action with a long cooldown from a damage preset still waited for combat. When the opener's first step was one of those (Machinist's Reassemble or Flamethrower before the first shot), the rotation targeted the enemy and then waited for an action it was never allowed to press, so the character stood at the target until it was pressed by hand. Now, while another plugin is in control and the chosen target is an enemy within 25 yalms, any self-usable action the damage rotation picks fires out of combat as part of the pull: the opener's buffs, and also a heal dump or shield the rotation chooses at that moment. An enemy further away is one the plugin is still travelling to, so buffs are not spent on it early. With no plugin in control, with no enemy targeted, or with the enemy out of reach, the out-of-combat rule is unchanged: heal dumps, shields and other self-only actions from a damage preset still wait for combat.

XIVCombo for very lazy players.","InternalName":"GluttonyCombo","AssemblyVersion":"1.0.4.324","Changelog":"v1.0.4.338 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v1.0.4.337 (2026-11-09) [testing]
- **The AI decision layer is gone.** The Fight Brain's question side - the raidwide mitigation ask, the pre-pull plan reader (party finder text and the `/gluttony plan` note command), and the party-callout reader - has been removed from the plugin, together with its relay address setting and the two "Plan Reader"/"Callout Reader" switches. GluttonyCombo no longer asks any decision model anything, sends no snapshot anywhere, and keeps no relay URL: the only network path it still uses is the movement tap's `/move/ingest` upload, which records the movement profiles and never carried a decision.
- What stays is pure code and unchanged: the rotation and every combo, the Fight Brain forecast reads and `FB|forecast` lines, the countdown strip, the shadow cast-gate lines, the party-data shadow rules (`FB|party-mit`, `FB|pos-zone`), and the movement recorder and shadow move planner. The move planner's `MP|` decision lines keep their exact format and now always carry the code pick only.
- The shadow move planner no longer has its ask-side toggle; `/gluttony movelog` now switches the recorder and the planner together, and its status line reads two switches instead of three.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.336 (2026-11-09) [testing]
- **Saving a custom action to a hotbar while in PvP now writes the PvP layout.** The custom-action editor's hotbar save told the game the write was a normal-slot write regardless of the current content, so a save made while in PvP updated the regular hotbar set instead of the PvP one; the call now passes the content check (upstream's fix), so the PvP variant of the slot is the one written.
- **The action-replacing hook answers in the game's own yes/no shape.** The IsActionIdReplaceable detour and its delegate declared an unsigned 64-bit return where the game's callback uses a boolean, so the replace decision relied on 0/1 marshalling to land correctly; both signatures now match the native BOOL return (upstream's fix), and the early-return values read true/false instead of 1/0. No behavior change is intended - this removes a latent hook-contract mismatch.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.335 (2026-11-07) [testing]
- **AoE heals no longer fire back to back on a party that is at or near full HP.** Follow-up to 1.0.4.334: on a party whose bars all read full or nearly full, the auto-rotation kept pressing AoE heals - a bar just under 100% never counted as full (regen-tick oscillation and display rounding), and a heal that had just gone out did not stand the press path down while it landed. Two changes, shared by Astrologian, White Mage, Scholar and Sage. First, a member only counts as needing an AoE heal on a real deficit: a bar at or above 98% reads as full for both the one-button average and the auto-rotation's member count, so no threshold setting (including the 100 "disable this check" setting, and a target count of 0, which is now floored at 1) can make a full party eligible. Second, the auto-rotation presses one AoE heal at a time: after a press goes out, the next waits out that cast's flight plus a second for the heal to land and party HP to propagate, so a movement-cancelled cast is no longer re-issued every tick. Real damage is never starved - a party still under the threshold after the window heals again immediately. Single-target heals, raidwide pre-casts and the 1.0.4.334 out-of-range fix are unchanged; the manual one-button still heals when pressed.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.334 (2026-11-07) [testing]
- **Healer one-button AoE heals no longer trigger off party members the heal cannot reach.** The Astrologian, White Mage, Scholar and Sage one-button AoE heal rotations averaged the whole party's HP: a member standing outside the heal's radius kept the average under the threshold, so the rotation kept choosing AoE heals (Helios, Medica, Succor, Prognosis and their oGCD neighbours) that could never heal that member. The trigger now averages only the members inside the heal's own effect radius (15y for the Helios family), alive and targetable, so the rotation returns to damaging while nobody reachable needs healing, and heals again the moment the far member comes back into range. Single-target healing is untouched: a member returning to range is picked up by the single-target path exactly as before. Raidwide pre-casts and the auto-rotation's own cast gate are unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.333 (2026-11-06) [testing]
- **The movement recorder and the shadow move planner actually start now.** Every load of 1.0.4.328-1.0.4.332 killed them at startup: the tap installed itself before the settings existed and died on an error the moment the plugin loaded, so no movement was recorded at all in any session and nothing reached the movement database. The tap now installs after the settings load, the settings read can no longer fail that way, and if an install ever fails again it retries on the framework tick and on every zone change (a login is one) instead of staying dead for the whole session.
- **The movement relay address can no longer be lost to a blank setting.** A blank relay address now falls back to the shared LAN Jev relay, so recorded movement reaches the database without anyone typing /gluttony movelog relay first; the command still overrides the address. Before this build a blank address silently switched the uploads off.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Log only: nothing moves the character, nothing presses a button, never in PvP, off under AutoDuty. 1.0.4.328-1.0.4.332 collected no movement samples; this is the first build that can.","RepoUrl":"https://github.com/dajoey/lalalazy/tree/main/src/GluttonyCombo","ApplicableVersion":"any","DalamudApiLevel":15,"IsHide":false,"IsTestingExclusive":false,"DownloadLinkTesting":"https://github.com/dajoey/lalalazy/releases/download/GluttonyCombo-v1.0.4.338/GluttonyCombo-testing.zip","DownloadLinkInstall":"https://github.com/dajoey/lalalazy/releases/download/GluttonyCombo-v1.0.4.324/GluttonyCombo.zip","DownloadLinkUpdate":"https://github.com/dajoey/lalalazy/releases/download/GluttonyCombo-v1.0.4.324/GluttonyCombo.zip","Tags":["combo","gluttony","wrath","wrathcombo","auto","autorotation","rotation","pve","pvp","lalalazy"],"CategoryTags":null,"IconUrl":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dajoey/lalalazy/main/LalaImages/gluttonycombo-icon.png","ImageUrls":[""],"DownloadCount":0,"LastUpdate":"1790560588","TestingAssemblyVersion":"1.0.4.338","TestingDalamudApiLevel":15}

{"Author":"dajoey","Name":"Gluttony Combo","Punchline":"Lalalazy fork of Wrath Combo - XIVCombo for very lazy players.","Description":"Gluttony Combo - lalalazy fork of Gluttony Combo. XIVCombo for very lazy players.","InternalName":"GluttonyCombo","AssemblyVersion":"1.0.4.324","Changelog":"v1.0.4.338 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v1.0.4.337 (2026-11-09) [testing]
- **The AI decision layer is gone.** The Fight Brain's question side - the raidwide mitigation ask, the pre-pull plan reader (party finder text and the `/gluttony plan` note command), and the party-callout reader - has been removed from the plugin, together with its relay address setting and the two "Plan Reader"/"Callout Reader" switches. GluttonyCombo no longer asks any decision model anything, sends no snapshot anywhere, and keeps no relay URL: the only network path it still uses is the movement tap's `/move/ingest` upload, which records the movement profiles and never carried a decision.
- What stays is pure code and unchanged: the rotation and every combo, the Fight Brain forecast reads and `FB|forecast` lines, the countdown strip, the shadow cast-gate lines, the party-data shadow rules (`FB|party-mit`, `FB|pos-zone`), and the movement recorder and shadow move planner. The move planner's `MP|` decision lines keep their exact format and now always carry the code pick only.
- The shadow move planner no longer has its ask-side toggle; `/gluttony movelog` now switches the recorder and the planner together, and its status line reads two switches instead of three.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.336 (2026-11-09) [testing]
- **Saving a custom action to a hotbar while in PvP now writes the PvP layout.** The custom-action editor's hotbar save told the game the write was a normal-slot write regardless of the current content, so a save made while in PvP updated the regular hotbar set instead of the PvP one; the call now passes the content check (upstream's fix), so the PvP variant of the slot is the one written.
- **The action-replacing hook answers in the game's own yes/no shape.** The IsActionIdReplaceable detour and its delegate declared an unsigned 64-bit return where the game's callback uses a boolean, so the replace decision relied on 0/1 marshalling to land correctly; both signatures now match the native BOOL return (upstream's fix), and the early-return values read true/false instead of 1/0. No behavior change is intended - this removes a latent hook-contract mismatch.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.335 (2026-11-07) [testing]
- **AoE heals no longer fire back to back on a party that is at or near full HP.** Follow-up to 1.0.4.334: on a party whose bars all read full or nearly full, the auto-rotation kept pressing AoE heals - a bar just under 100% never counted as full (regen-tick oscillation and display rounding), and a heal that had just gone out did not stand the press path down while it landed. Two changes, shared by Astrologian, White Mage, Scholar and Sage. First, a member only counts as needing an AoE heal on a real deficit: a bar at or above 98% reads as full for both the one-button average and the auto-rotation's member count, so no threshold setting (including the 100 "disable this check" setting, and a target count of 0, which is now floored at 1) can make a full party eligible. Second, the auto-rotation presses one AoE heal at a time: after a press goes out, the next waits out that cast's flight plus a second for the heal to land and party HP to propagate, so a movement-cancelled cast is no longer re-issued every tick. Real damage is never starved - a party still under the threshold after the window heals again immediately. Single-target heals, raidwide pre-casts and the 1.0.4.334 out-of-range fix are unchanged; the manual one-button still heals when pressed.

v1.0.4.337 (2026-11-09) [testing]
- **The AI decision layer is gone.** The Fight Brain's question side - the raidwide mitigation ask, the pre-pull plan reader (party finder text and the `/gluttony plan` note command), and the party-callout reader - has been removed from the plugin, together with its relay address setting and the two "Plan Reader"/"Callout Reader" switches. GluttonyCombo no longer asks any decision model anything, sends no snapshot anywhere, and keeps no relay URL: the only network path it still uses is the movement tap's `/move/ingest` upload, which records the movement profiles and never carried a decision.
- What stays is pure code and unchanged: the rotation and every combo, the Fight Brain forecast reads and `FB|forecast` lines, the countdown strip, the shadow cast-gate lines, the party-data shadow rules (`FB|party-mit`, `FB|pos-zone`), and the movement recorder and shadow move planner. The move planner's `MP|` decision lines keep their exact format and now always carry the code pick only.
- The shadow move planner no longer has its ask-side toggle; `/gluttony movelog` now switches the recorder and the planner together, and its status line reads two switches instead of three.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.336 (2026-11-09) [testing]
- **Saving a custom action to a hotbar while in PvP now writes the PvP layout.** The custom-action editor's hotbar save told the game the write was a normal-slot write regardless of the current content, so a save made while in PvP updated the regular hotbar set instead of the PvP one; the call now passes the content check (upstream's fix), so the PvP variant of the slot is the one written.
- **The action-replacing hook answers in the game's own yes/no shape.** The IsActionIdReplaceable detour and its delegate declared an unsigned 64-bit return where the game's callback uses a boolean, so the replace decision relied on 0/1 marshalling to land correctly; both signatures now match the native BOOL return (upstream's fix), and the early-return values read true/false instead of 1/0. No behavior change is intended - this removes a latent hook-contract mismatch.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.335 (2026-11-07) [testing]
- **AoE heals no longer fire back to back on a party that is at or near full HP.** Follow-up to 1.0.4.334: on a party whose bars all read full or nearly full, the auto-rotation kept pressing AoE heals - a bar just under 100% never counted as full (regen-tick oscillation and display rounding), and a heal that had just gone out did not stand the press path down while it landed. Two changes, shared by Astrologian, White Mage, Scholar and Sage. First, a member only counts as needing an AoE heal on a real deficit: a bar at or above 98% reads as full for both the one-button average and the auto-rotation's member count, so no threshold setting (including the 100 "disable this check" setting, and a target count of 0, which is now floored at 1) can make a full party eligible. Second, the auto-rotation presses one AoE heal at a time: after a press goes out, the next waits out that cast's flight plus a second for the heal to land and party HP to propagate, so a movement-cancelled cast is no longer re-issued every tick. Real damage is never starved - a party still under the threshold after the window heals again immediately. Single-target heals, raidwide pre-casts and the 1.0.4.334 out-of-range fix are unchanged; the manual one-button still heals when pressed.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.334 (2026-11-07) [testing]
- **Healer one-button AoE heals no longer trigger off party members the heal cannot reach.** The Astrologian, White Mage, Scholar and Sage one-button AoE heal rotations averaged the whole party's HP: a member standing outside the heal's radius kept the average under the threshold, so the rotation kept choosing AoE heals (Helios, Medica, Succor, Prognosis and their oGCD neighbours) that could never heal that member. The trigger now averages only the members inside the heal's own effect radius (15y for the Helios family), alive and targetable, so the rotation returns to damaging while nobody reachable needs healing, and heals again the moment the far member comes back into range. Single-target healing is untouched: a member returning to range is picked up by the single-target path exactly as before. Raidwide pre-casts and the auto-rotation's own cast gate are unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.333 (2026-11-06) [testing]
- **The movement recorder and the shadow move planner actually start now.** Every load of 1.0.4.328-1.0.4.332 killed them at startup: the tap installed itself before the settings existed and died on an error the moment the plugin loaded, so no movement was recorded at all in any session and nothing reached the movement database. The tap now installs after the settings load, the settings read can no longer fail that way, and if an install ever fails again it retries on the framework tick and on every zone change (a login is one) instead of staying dead for the whole session.
- **The movement relay address can no longer be lost to a blank setting.** A blank relay address now falls back to the shared LAN Jev relay, so recorded movement reaches the database without anyone typing /gluttony movelog relay first; the command still overrides the address. Before this build a blank address silently switched the uploads off.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. d2ea413: feat: use a divination-deploy App token instead of DEPLOY_GITHUB_TOKEN (#799)

reusable-deploy-plugin.yml checks out the distribution repository, opens
a pull request there and merges it. Mint a GitHub App installation token
scoped to that repository instead of using a bot PAT.

Drop the Authorization header when fetching commits.json. This
repository is public so the request needs no authentication, and
expanding a token on the command line exposes it through the process
list.

Reference the reusable workflow by local path. Pinning it by SHA means a
change here does not take effect until every caller is updated, which
would leave a broken intermediate state whenever a secret is renamed.

Drop the explicit create-pull-request author: it defaults to
github.actor, which attributes the deployment to whoever triggered it.

{"Author":"dexcss","Name":"Glamour Sorter","AcceptsFeedback":true,"ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"1.3.0.19","CategoryTags":["Utility","Inventory"],"Changelog":"v1.3.0.19: Spare copies are no longer planned as stores — a piece whose appearance is already in the dresser is dropped from the set plan and reported as a duplicate (the bag copy can be sold), which also removes the HQ leftovers that made the game refuse outfit stores. Skipped sets are always reported now (1.3.0.18 dropped them from the result list), and the plan card note text is fixed. v1.3.0.18: Outfit stores now hand in NQ pieces only — every HQ hand-in made the game refuse the combination silently (all successful stores in the 21:15-21:30 run used NQ pieces, all refusals involved HQ). HQ-only sets are reported as \"the dresser will not take HQ gear as an outfit glamour\" instead of failing after a click. Slot diagnostics also show each planned piece's quality. v1.3.0.17: Failed outfit stores now report the game's own reason — chat messages printed during the attempt are logged under \"game said:\" and the result reads \"The game did not accept this outfit (left for manual review)\", so the remaining refusals can be identified exactly instead of guessed. v1.3.0.16: Confirmation now clicks the real Yes button first (what a player does), then falls back to callback event 2 and event 0 in stages — the seasonal dialog was closing without depositing when only callbacks were fired. Combined with 1.3.0.15, \"already in the stored outfit\" is reported as ALREADY and is no longer counted as a store. v1.3.0.15: Honest results — \"Already in the stored outfit — nothing to add\" is now its own ALREADY state and no longer counts as a successful store; the tally reads stored / already there / need attention / failed. The store step also logs the click and, if no confirmation opens within 2 s, fires the addon's Store as Glamour callback (18) before giving up. v1.3.0.14: Diagnosis + fallback for the seasonal Outfit Glamour Creation stalls — the store step now logs the addon state, hand-in counts and every slot (item id, inventory type, flag), and if no confirmation opens within 2 s it fires the addon's Store as Glamour callback (18) as a fallback. v1.3.0.13: Quality consistency for outfit hand-ins — the outfit window only accepts pieces of one quality (\"Only items of the same quality may be selected\") and a mixed HQ/NQ selection made the game silently refuse the store while leaving the window open. The plugin now anchors on the quality it holds most of and hands in only pieces of that quality, logging any piece skipped for quality. v1.3.0.12: Checkbox-dialog fix — the confirm ladder now ticks the \"Store as Outfit Glamour\" checkbox first (synthetic ButtonClick + SetChecked) and fires Yes once the game enables it, instead of firing the default-confirm callback first, which closed the dialog without depositing on several sets (the \"checkbox was never selected\" symptom). The default-confirm callback is kept as a fallback for dialogs whose Yes cannot be enabled from the checkbox. v1.3.0.11: Cross-set outfit mismatch guard — a glamour piece can belong to more than one outfit set, and the game may open a different set's stored outfit when completing; the plugin now compares the opened outfit's item id with the planned set and skips with \"left for manual review\" instead of handing the piece into the wrong outfit and reporting a false failure. The store log keeps the dialog mode and prism-box index so any remaining case is diagnosable. v1.3.0.10: Fix the \"No deposit detected\" failures on outfit completions. The hand-in loop was allowed to target a slot already marked Filled (the outfit already contained that piece), which the game silently refused; it now only hands into Unfilled slots, and a set whose planned pieces are all already inside the outfit reports \"Already in the stored outfit — nothing to add\" instead of attempting a store. The native StoreExistingOutfit retry from 1.3.0.9 is removed — it returns success but deposits nothing unless the Glamour Creation window drives it. v1.3.0.9: Fix false \"No deposit detected\" results when completing an outfit — the game's confirm dialog sometimes closes without depositing for outfits that were only just created. After 1.5 s without a change the plugin now sends the same request the dialog sends (StoreExistingOutfit/StoreNewOutfit) once, then re-checks; store logs also report the dialog mode and prism-box index for diagnosis. v1.3.0.8: Withdraw tab clarity — the action buttons now state what they will do and grey out with an explicit empty-state label: \"No duplicates to withdraw\", \"No singles to withdraw\", and \"No sets to withdraw & re-deposit\" when there is nothing to pack (otherwise \"Withdraw & re-deposit sets (N)\" with counts). The consolidation description now explains the withdraw-then-pack-as-outfit loop and the slot saving. v1.3.0.7: Fix a window render crash when the set-consolidation loop ran with no loose set pieces left to start (the empty candidate list was indexed directly) — it now reports \"Nothing to consolidate\" instead. The consolidation pump is also exception-guarded so a future error cannot take the whole window down. v1.3.0.6: Set consolidation now runs in bag-sized batches — it withdraws one set's loose pieces (only as many as your free bag slots can hold), stores that set as a single outfit glamour, then repeats automatically. Before this the button tried to withdraw every loose set piece at once (359 items against 63 free slots) and was refused. v1.3.0.5: Dresser-full handling — at 800/800 the store run now stops with a clear 'Glamour Dresser is full' result instead of failing every remaining item with 'no deposit detected'. New \"set pieces stored loose\" detector on the Withdraw tab: it finds items the dresser stores individually that belong to an outfit set, shows how many pieces/sets and the approximate slots that would be freed, withdraws them (arm-then-confirm), then automatically runs the store pass that packs each set into one outfit glamour. v1.3.0.4: Single-item deposits now work — loose glamour items (not part of an outfit set) are stored with the game's own prism-box request command (the same request the Glamour Creation window's Yes button sends) instead of trying to open the outfit-store window, which the game only opens for set items. Each item costs one glamour prism (checked first) and the result reports \"Stored item (dresser X->Y)\". Outfit sets keep the existing flow. v1.3.0.3: Withdraw fix — the extractor was waiting on the dresser's 'requested' flag, which stays set while the data is loaded, so a run could stop before sending anything (\"the dresser data stayed busy\"); it now only gates on the loaded flag and retries refused sends. Store: the hand-in window is allowed to finish populating before the fill step decides nothing can be handed over. UI: two pages — Deposit (scan/store) and Withdraw (extractor) — with Abort reachable on the active page. v1.3.0.2: Gear-set protection hardening — items saved in a gear set are now detected from the saved gearset entries as well as the game's gear-set icon check (a 1.3.0.0 test scan saw 110 protected pieces on one pass and only 1 on another, so a piece could be misfiled as sortable). Deposit verification now reads the dresser list from MirageManager, so a dresser window that is momentarily unreadable no longer turns a successful deposit into a false \"couldn't read the dresser\" warning. v1.3.0.1: Fixes from the first 1.3.0.0 test. The dresser's \"Add to pre-existing outfit glamour?\" Yes/No prompt (shown when completing a stored outfit) is now answered automatically — before this it left the store flow stuck with the prompt on screen and froze the run. The Abort button stays clickable while a run is in progress. New watchdogs stop a set whose store window never opens or never produces its confirmation instead of stalling the rest of the run. Extractor: a refused RestorePrismBoxItem is retried (the client briefly refuses while a previous restore settles), waits for the dresser data request to finish, and skips further copies of a unique item (the game cannot give you a second copy while you hold one) instead of stopping the whole run; log lines now name the refused item. v1.3.0.0: Loose items — glamour-able items that belong to no outfit set are now stored as well, one at a time, and skipped when that item is already anywhere in the dresser. Extractor — withdraw dresser items back into your bags: all loose items, duplicates only (keeps one of each), or one item or item type such as all rings, with a live progress line. Item names and icons — planned pieces, duplicates and results now show the item icon, name and category instead of a raw item id. v1.2.0.1: Audit fixes. Completing an existing outfit works again — the pieces a stored outfit is still missing are planned as needed and are no longer listed as sellable duplicates. Deposit verification also accepts the planned pieces leaving your bags, so completing an outfit (or storing with a nearly full dresser) reports correctly instead of \"No deposit detected\". Store steps can no longer drop a set silently when a window does not open or the dresser closes mid-run, the store loop retries briefly while the dresser data reloads instead of stopping the rest of the run, and the Armoire toggle is locked while storing. /xllog now logs the scanned dresser/held counts for troubleshooting. v1.2.0.0: Full audit. Gear-set protection — pieces registered to a saved gear set are now left in your bags (the same check the game uses for its gear-set icon mark), instead of being pulled out of your gear sets. Smarter duplicates — stored outfit glamours are expanded into their pieces, so a second copy of an already-stored piece is flagged as sellable instead of being re-stored. The dresser's expanded item list is scanned, and a never-fill guard skips window slots the game already marks as part of the stored outfit. New model-duplicate hints show when a planned piece shares its appearance with something already stored. Deposit verification now retries briefly instead of failing on a single read. UI: version in the title, live progress tally while storing, MANUAL tag priority, gear-set and model-duplicate sections. Removed diagnostic logging. v1.1.1.0: The Store as Outfit Glamour checkbox dialog is now automated (synthetic checkbox click + default-confirm callback); all sets route to the dresser. v1.1.0.0: Armoire routing added.","DalamudApiLevel":15,"Description":"Sorts glamour-able gear from your inventory into the Glamour Dresser — outfit sets as outfit glamours (including seasonal sets, with the Store as Outfit Glamour checkbox dialog automated) and loose items one by one — skipping anything already stored. {"Author":"dajoey","Name":"Gluttony Combo","ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"1.0.4.324","CategoryTags":null,"Changelog":"v1.0.4.326 (2026-11-03) [testing]
- **Action replacement follows the game's own hook plumbing again.** Upstream WrathCombo replaced its hand-written hook delegate with the game's GetAdjustedActionId delegate type and reads the action manager through the game's accessor at call time instead of a pointer cached at startup, so action replacement keeps working when the game moves or re-creates the action manager; that upstream change (1e64c866) is merged. The fork's replacement behavior, throttle, mandragora hold and error reporting are unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.325 (2026-11-02) [testing]
- **Treasure dungeons: no AoE while the mandragora pack is alive.** The five mandragoras (onion, egg, garlic, tomato, queen) in the treasure dungeons have to die one at a time, in order, for the full reward, and an AoE on the clumped pack breaks the order. While any of them is alive, the auto-rotation runs its single-target rotation only, and any action that can hit more than one enemy is held: cleaves, circles, cones, lines and ground areas (Circle of Scorn, Glare IV, Flare Star, Salted Earth and the like, including damage-and-heal actions such as Assize), plus actions whose follow-up is an AoE (Standard Step and Technical Step, the primal summons and Enkindles, Living Shadow). A held weave is skipped; a held GCD is replaced by the button's current single-target action (Glare IV becomes Glare III, Standard Step becomes Cascade), and readiness checks report held actions as not ready so rotations move on to their next priority. The same applies to single-target buttons pressed by hand. Heals, mitigation (Reprisal included) and party buffs are not held, and an AoE button pressed by hand still does what it says. Normal rotation resumes as soon as the last mandragora is dead. Covers the Hidden and Lost Canals of Uznair, the Shifting Altars of Uznair, both Lyhe Ghiah dungeons, the Excitatron 6000, the Shifting Gymnasion Agonon, Cenote Ja Ja Gural and the Vault Oneiron.
- A dance already in progress when the pack appears cannot finish until the pack is dead, because its finish is an AoE.
- A held GCD with no single-target action on its button waits instead: Red Mage holds Grand Impact, and while Grand Impact is ready the game shows it in place of Jolt III, so that GCD waits until the pack is dead or the buff ends (instant casts, Verstone, Verfire and the melee combo still go; a hand press of that button does nothing meanwhile).
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.324 (2026-11-02) [testing]
- **A pull started by another plugin no longer stalls on the opener's first self-buff.** While a plugin such as Henchman, AutoDuty or Lazy Fate Automation drives the rotation, the out-of-combat restriction already lifted for attacks, but a self-only action with a long cooldown from a damage preset still waited for combat. When the opener's first step was one of those (Machinist's Reassemble or Flamethrower before the first shot), the rotation targeted the enemy and then waited for an action it was never allowed to press, so the character stood at the target until it was pressed by hand. Now, while another plugin is in control and the chosen target is an enemy within 25 yalms, any self-usable action the damage rotation picks fires out of combat as part of the pull: the opener's buffs, and also a heal dump or shield the rotation chooses at that moment. An enemy further away is one the plugin is still travelling to, so buffs are not spent on it early. With no plugin in control, with no enemy targeted, or with the enemy out of reach, the out-of-combat rule is unchanged: heal dumps, shields and other self-only actions from a damage preset still wait for combat.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.323 (2026-11-01) [testing]
- **A cancelled heal cast is no longer counted as a completed one.** The healer raidwide locks (White Mage Medica II/Medica III, Astrologian Aspected Helios/Helios Conjunction, Scholar Succor/Concitation) treated "the cast bar was up and then went away" as a finished cast: a cast cancelled a moment in marked the timed regen as owning that raidwide for its whole duration and started the raidwide-shield cooldown, so the heal was never re-cast for the hit. Completion is now the action actually registering as used, so a cancelled cast is claimed and re-cast, and a finished cast still releases the lock exactly as before.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.322 (2026-10-28) [testing]
- **BossMod status checks survive a missing or half-loaded BossMod.** Upstream WrathCombo reorganized its BossMod IPC into shared helpers with null-safe fallbacks; that rework (d9c63e468) is merged, so the active-preset module walk, autorotation, custom-queueing, smart-target and AI-targeting checks answer false cleanly when BossMod's rotation window or action queue is absent, instead of erroring partway through the walk.
- BossMod Reborn keeps being read through its own IPC (active preset verdict, AI targeting, manual-queue setting); those reads are unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.321 (2026-10-27) [testing]
- **BossMod conflict detection works with current BossMod builds again.** BossMod moved its rotation manager and action-module queue underneath a new window object, so the checks that read the original BossMod's active preset, AI targeting and manual-queue setting found nothing and the preset, AI-targeting and manual-queue verdicts silently came back empty. {"Author":"dajoey","Name":"Gluttony Combo","ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"1.0.4.324","CategoryTags":null,"Changelog":"v1.0.4.326 (2026-11-03) [testing]
- **Action replacement follows the game's own hook plumbing again.** Upstream WrathCombo replaced its hand-written hook delegate with the game's GetAdjustedActionId delegate type and reads the action manager through the game's accessor at call time instead of a pointer cached at startup, so action replacement keeps working when the game moves or re-creates the action manager; that upstream change (1e64c866) is merged. The fork's replacement behavior, throttle, mandragora hold and error reporting are unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.325 (2026-11-02) [testing]
- **Treasure dungeons: no AoE while the mandragora pack is alive.** The five mandragoras (onion, egg, garlic, tomato, queen) in the treasure dungeons have to die one at a time, in order, for the full reward, and an AoE on the clumped pack breaks the order. While any of them is alive, the auto-rotation runs its single-target rotation only, and any action that can hit more than one enemy is held: cleaves, circles, cones, lines and ground areas (Circle of Scorn, Glare IV, Flare Star, Salted Earth and the like, including damage-and-heal actions such as Assize), plus actions whose follow-up is an AoE (Standard Step and Technical Step, the primal summons and Enkindles, Living Shadow). A held weave is skipped; a held GCD is replaced by the button's current single-target action (Glare IV becomes Glare III, Standard Step becomes Cascade), and readiness checks report held actions as not ready so rotations move on to their next priority. The same applies to single-target buttons pressed by hand. Heals, mitigation (Reprisal included) and party buffs are not held, and an AoE button pressed by hand still does what it says. Normal rotation resumes as soon as the last mandragora is dead. Covers the Hidden and Lost Canals of Uznair, the Shifting Altars of Uznair, both Lyhe Ghiah dungeons, the Excitatron 6000, the Shifting Gymnasion Agonon, Cenote Ja Ja Gural and the Vault Oneiron.
- A dance already in progress when the pack appears cannot finish until the pack is dead, because its finish is an AoE.
- A held GCD with no single-target action on its button waits instead: Red Mage holds Grand Impact, and while Grand Impact is ready the game shows it in place of Jolt III, so that GCD waits until the pack is dead or the buff ends (instant casts, Verstone, Verfire and the melee combo still go; a hand press of that button does nothing meanwhile).
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.324 (2026-11-02) [testing]
- **A pull started by another plugin no longer stalls on the opener's first self-buff.** While a plugin such as Henchman, AutoDuty or Lazy Fate Automation drives the rotation, the out-of-combat restriction already lifted for attacks, but a self-only action with a long cooldown from a damage preset still waited for combat. When the opener's first step was one of those (Machinist's Reassemble or Flamethrower before the first shot), the rotation targeted the enemy and then waited for an action it was never allowed to press, so the character stood at the target until it was pressed by hand. Now, while another plugin is in control and the chosen target is an enemy within 25 yalms, any self-usable action the damage rotation picks fires out of combat as part of the pull: the opener's buffs, and also a heal dump or shield the rotation chooses at that moment. An enemy further away is one the plugin is still travelling to, so buffs are not spent on it early. With no plugin in control, with no enemy targeted, or with the enemy out of reach, the out-of-combat rule is unchanged: heal dumps, shields and other self-only actions from a damage preset still wait for combat.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.323 (2026-11-01) [testing]
- **A cancelled heal cast is no longer counted as a completed one.** The healer raidwide locks (White Mage Medica II/Medica III, Astrologian Aspected Helios/Helios Conjunction, Scholar Succor/Concitation) treated "the cast bar was up and then went away" as a finished cast: a cast cancelled a moment in marked the timed regen as owning that raidwide for its whole duration and started the raidwide-shield cooldown, so the heal was never re-cast for the hit. Completion is now the action actually registering as used, so a cancelled cast is claimed and re-cast, and a finished cast still releases the lock exactly as before.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.322 (2026-10-28) [testing]
- **BossMod status checks survive a missing or half-loaded BossMod.** Upstream WrathCombo reorganized its BossMod IPC into shared helpers with null-safe fallbacks; that rework (d9c63e468) is merged, so the active-preset module walk, autorotation, custom-queueing, smart-target and AI-targeting checks answer false cleanly when BossMod's rotation window or action queue is absent, instead of erroring partway through the walk.
- BossMod Reborn keeps being read through its own IPC (active preset verdict, AI targeting, manual-queue setting); those reads are unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.321 (2026-10-27) [testing]
- **BossMod conflict detection works with current BossMod builds again.** BossMod moved its rotation manager and action-module queue underneath a new window object, so the checks that read the original BossMod's active preset, AI targeting and manual-queue setting found nothing and the preset, AI-targeting and manual-queue verdicts silently came back empty. Those reflection reads now follow the new location, and upstream WrathCombo's matching fix (54e36f2f) is merged; BossMod Reborn keeps being read through its own IPC and is unchanged.

{"Author":"croizat, dajoey","Name":"Lazy Fate Automation","ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"0.0.3.10","CategoryTags":["utility"],"Changelog":"v0.0.3.10 (2026-10-31) [testing]
- **The FATE grind no longer starts FATEs above your level.** Level sync only lowers your level to match a FATE, it never raises it, so a FATE above your level could not be contributed to and walking to it only wasted time. FATEs above your level are now skipped; the tracker's unavailable list shows "FATE level N is above your level M". FATEs at or below your level run exactly as before.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.0.3.9 (2026-10-18) [testing]
- **Display name format and sort order changes are now saved.** Edits in the FATE tracker's "Sorting & Display" settings previously lived only in memory and reverted on the next plugin load; every change now persists immediately.
- **Reset to Default restores the actual default sort order.** The reset button dropped the Time Remaining criterion and put Time Remaining Urgent in ascending order (urgent FATEs last); it now restores the shipped six-entry default, shared with the config's own default so the two cannot drift apart.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.0.3.8 (2026-10-13) [testing]
- **BossMod Reborn no longer runs its own job rotations beside Gluttony Combo during FATEs.** The FATE grind creates and uses its own BossMod preset, "LazyFateAutomation", holding only the movement, FATE-targeting, level-sync and stay-close-to-target modules (melee and tanks close in, other roles hold at 10 yalms), and rewrites it each time the grind starts so an old or edited copy cannot bring job rotations back.
- **The grind no longer clears a BossMod preset another plugin (such as AutoDuty) or the player set.** It turns its preset on and off with BossMod Reborn's standard preset calls and only ever clears its own. Two calls BossMod Reborn does not provide, which failed on every attempt, are gone, and a failing call is logged once per run.
- The BossMod preset named "Gluttony" that earlier versions created is no longer used. It is left untouched in BossMod's preset list and can be deleted there by hand.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.0.3.7 (2026-10-05) [testing]
- **The boss FATE icon on the server info bar entry now actually renders.** The previous testing build showed no icon at all because the glyph reference pointed at an empty slot instead of the boss FATE icon; the icon value is now pinned so it stays the boss glyph.

{"Author":"Akari","Name":"Mahjong Advisor","AcceptsFeedback":true,"ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"0.4.4.0","CanUnloadAsync":false,"CategoryTags":["Utility"],"Changelog":"v0.4.4.0: Chi picker freeze fix. When a call prompt's claimed tile could not be identified, the single-shape chi gate counted shapes for the wrong tile: each candidate offered one run, but the actual tile completed two, so the game opened its shape-selection dialog - which ignores call callbacks - and the match froze (live at South 4 while leading 38,400; bundle 20261030-081345). Chi now fires only when the claim is pinned to one tile, or when every tile that could legally be on offer completes exactly one run; anything else passes instead. The picker-stall warning also logs once rather than every frame. The stale Advisor block that earlier builds wrote into the plugin config is no longer serialised: it was never read, is ignored on load, and disappears at the next config save. An experimental rollout-search re-ranking of discard candidates is included but ships OFF: a 240-match paired simulator A/B (two seeds) rejected it - it traded a 39% relative win-rate drop for nothing - so it stays a foundation for later work. v0.4.3.0: Result-screen retry. The result panel can swallow the first advance callback while it animates; the controller fired it twice and then its acted guard blocked every retry, leaving the screen waiting indefinitely (live Advanced freeze, state 29 unresolved for 12s). Advances now retry every 2.5 seconds while the result state persists, capped at 8 attempts so the deliberately manual match-end screen is not spammed. v0.4.2.0: Match-level tuning. A full hanchan evaluator now plays East+South with real score accounting, dealer rotation, honcha, riichi sticks and placement, and 120 paired matches showed the old risk settings were too passive. Win value 1800 and deal-in cost 4000 beat 1300/5200 on identical deals (average place 2.55 vs 2.65, more firsts, fewer fourths) with the deal-in rate unchanged at 9.3%. A v7 config migration applies the new values. Riichi hand value and placement stance were also tested and left unchanged - both were flat across 60-match arms. v0.4.1.0: Advanced-table defence. Cross-seat genbutsu now uses the pond lengths captured at the instant a riichi marker appears; the old turn-count shortcut broke once calls shortened ponds and could mark a tile discarded before the riichi as safe. Two declared riichi also force a fold for any hand that is not tenpai, overriding the placement chase. The simulator now records the same declaration snapshots: over 1,000 hands the defence fix moved deal-in rate from 10.3% to 9.5% and average points from -22 to +17, while the double-riichi rail was neutral there because the simulation has no placement stance. Live Advanced trial on 0.4.0.0 finished 1st, 4th, then leading when stopped; the 4th lost two deal-ins to one riichi player, the second 12,000 while two were in riichi. v0.4.0.0: Exact scoring core. Completed hands are now scored by yaku, fu, dora and the payment table (closed and open, riichi through yakuman), and the offline simulator uses that scoring for win legality and payouts. Ready-hand valuation was built and benchmarked but stays out of live decisions: over 1,500 simulated hands, mixing exact tenpai values with the existing one-away estimate cut the win rate from 15.4% to 8.1%, so the value scale must be unified for every shanten first. Advice is memoised per table state so the overlay and controller do not recompute the same decision. v0.3.10.0: Silent-endgame defence. The threat model measured a silent opponent as at most 19% likely tenpai, so on a table with no riichi and no melds every safety rule stayed off - the controller pushed one-away hands with 6-9 tiles left to draw into damaten twice in one match (4,200 and 2,200 deal-ins) and paid full tsumo on 14,300 and 20,000 hands. Silent seats now take on a readiness floor that rises from zero at wall 32 to a concrete threat at wall 16, arming the existing late-wall fold and per-tile safety ranking on quiet tables. v0.3.9.0: Chi freeze fixed. The shape-selection dialog ignores scripted call picks (confirmed by the first picker dump), so chi now only fires when exactly one shape is possible - that path completes with no dialog. Multi-shape chi passes instead of stalling; the pass log records how many shapes were declined. v0.3.8.0: Late-wall defence. When an opponent is a concrete threat and the wall is down to the last four go-arounds, the controller folds any hand that is not tenpai instead of pushing a 1-shanten no-riichi hand. This was the 12,000 deal-in in the first match. Diagnostic bundles now also include chi picker dumps. The end-of-match results screen still waits for you by design - that is the one click after a match. v0.3.7.0: Chi is now fully automated. The controller calls chi when the advisor ranks it best, and if the client shows the shape-selection surface it fires the first variant and re-evaluates the hand. The picker layout is dumped once per session to the log folder so shape-specific selection can be refined against real captures. A v6 config migration enables chi. v0.3.6.0: Read each opponent meld strip independently. A hidden empty strip for one quiet seat no longer suppresses every visible meld on the table, so the threat model sees called sets when they exist. This is a readiness/defence accuracy change; automation logic is unchanged. v0.3.5.0: Fix the second freeze. A complete open hand is no longer assumed to be a legal tsumo: the controller checks for an actual yaku and keeps discarding when there is none. Call prompts now prefer the newest board addition over a possibly stale pond tile (the live log claimed 6z/dragon while the actual Pon was 9m), and the log records the last discard tile/seat. A v5 config migration re-enables auto-play/logging. v0.3.4.0: Fix the self-kan freeze. A Kan/Pass bar at state 6 is ignored and the normal discard proceeds instead of firing a Pass callback the client ignores. Session stats are preserved after /mjadv stop so the bundle still shows the run, and a v4 config migration re-enables auto-play/logging for the next launch. v0.3.3.0: Reset the exposed tuning sliders to the fitted win-rate defaults (base hand value 1300, deal-in 5200, noten 1500, opponent hand 4000) with a one-time v3 config migration. Diagnostic bundles now include the actual Dalamud plugin config file from pluginConfigs. v0.3.2.0: State 15 is now treated as the generic other-players state unless real call buttons are present, state 22 (forced riichi discard) is automated, and state 27 (between-hands result/score) is recognised instead of showing stale advice. Overlay/advice are now gated to actual decision states, and diagnostic bundles can read the Dalamud log while it is open. v0.3.1.0: Auto-play and file logging are now on by default, /mjadv session starts a clean logged session, and /mjadv bundle packages the recent JSONL logs, config, layouts, Dalamud log tail and a full last-read snapshot into one zip. Status changes are now logged as auto-status records. v0.3.0.1: Re-arm auto-play on a state change even when the hand happens to repeat, and wait for the Riichi/Pass prompt to close before cutting the riichi tile. v0.3.0.0: Optional auto-play. Replays the client's FireCallback protocol for discards, calls, riichi, ron/tsumo and result advancement, using the reference solver's live-verified handshake and timing guards. Off by default; /mjadv auto [on/off] or /mjadv stop toggles it. Pon/ron/tsumo/riichi are enabled by default, chi and kan are opt-in, the chi shape picker pauses for a manual choice, and the new-hand screen is never auto-advanced. Added /mjadv hand and /mjadv options diagnostics. v0.2.0.2: Keep the previous wall count, so the wall-jump half of new-hand detection actually fires. v0.2.0.1: Reset the pond baselines at the start of a new hand, so the first discard of the hand is tracked and the first call prompt gets the right claimed tile. v0.2.0.0: Meld containers now read by default (112-115 families), with a fail-closed check against our own called-meld count. Own meld tiles are recovered from hand deltas when nodes are unavailable, so ukeire no longer counts tiles already in a call. Riichi detection is marker-node only; the dead rotation and score-drop paths are gone. One node-tree walk per read instead of up to seven. Fixed dead hands getting a nonzero win rate and Pass inventing a yaku path. Red-five decoding accepts both absolute and alias ids. Removed the obsolete fold-threshold setting. Setup window no longer reopens every launch. Added /mjadv melds diagnostics and richer log records.","DalamudApiLevel":15,"Description":"Reads your Doman Mahjong hand, discards, dora, scores and called melds, then ranks each discard by hand speed against deal-in risk. {"Author":"dajoey","Name":"PvP Solver","ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"0.1.1.2","CategoryTags":null,"Changelog":"v0.1.2.10 (2026-11-01) [testing]
- **The per-job defensive actions also read real HP.** Heart of Corundum, Tempera Coat, Earth's Reply, Riddle of Earth, the Bloodbath rows, Lady of Crowns, Microcosmos, Meisui, Impalement, Xenoglossy's low-HP arm and Shadowbringer's HP arm compared their "use below this HP" thresholds against predicted HP, which counts heals still on the way; predicted can read 84% one second before a death at about 40% real HP. They now compare against the current HP out of the maximum, the same real value Guard and the defensive table already use. Thresholds and defaults are unchanged, and reads of enemies' and allies' HP (Smite, Guardian, Blasting Zone, Perfectio, the burst target) are untouched.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.2.9 (2026-11-01) [testing]
- **Self-defence now reads real HP.** Guard, Recuperate and the generic defensive actions (the "use below X% HP" table) compared their thresholds against predicted HP, which counts heals still on the way; predicted can read 84% one second before a death at about 40% real HP, so nothing fired. All of them now compare against the current HP out of the maximum, the same real value the Jev snapshot uses. Thresholds and defaults are unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.2.8 (2026-10-31) [testing]
- **"Let Jev call the shots" now sees real HP.** The player's and allies' HP sent to Jev is the current HP out of the maximum, no longer PvP Solver's predicted HP, which counts heals still on the way. In one match Jev was told 84% one second before a death at about 40%.
- **Jev's pick no longer drops when Jev is briefly unsure.** The relay now keeps the last pick itself while that enemy is still hittable, and drops it on purpose when the enemy goes under Guard, out of reach or stale. PvP Solver follows the relay's call and never brings a dropped pick back. Only with an older relay does PvP Solver keep the last pick, for up to three seconds after Jev gave it, while that enemy is still a valid target.
- **The Limit Break log matches what happened.** `JV|lb-fired` is written once when the Limit Break goes off in a fire window. `JV|lb-fire-skip` is written only when a window closes without it, with the reason: unusable, follow-up, out-of-range, no-target or timeout. A report of the use that arrives up to two seconds late still counts as fired. Before, a skip line could appear in windows that then fired, and windows that really failed wrote nothing.
- **Each action used is reported once.** The game reports each action twice; the same action on the same target within 1.5 seconds now counts once in the snapshot.
- **Alliance members are included (Frontline).** After the party members, the nearest alliance members are sent too, marked as alliance, up to eight allies in all. Each ally now carries its object id, so Jev can name an ally to heal.
- **Healer call, logged only.** When Jev suggests whom a healer should heal (an ally, self, attack or Guard), the suggestion is written as one `JV|heal-shadow` log line for the first suggestion in each fight and each time it changes; an answer with no suggestion does not count as a change. Nothing acts on it yet.
- **Relay failures are visible in the log.** One summary line per fight (when combat ends, or every 60 seconds while calls fail) counts calls that succeeded, timed out, got an error reply or failed. No line per call, and no call is counted in a later fight. An unreadable heal or Limit Break value in a reply no longer drops the rest of the answer.
- PvP Solver still never moves the character.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.1.2.7 (2026-10-29) [testing]
- **"Let Jev call the shots" reports what actually happened.** Each snapshot also carries the player's current target and the actions actually used since the last one (action and target only), so each of Jev's picks can be checked against what PvP Solver did and whether that enemy went down.
- Jev's focus pick is kept steady: it moves to another enemy only when that one is clearly the better pick.
- **A line, cone or splash Limit Break that Jev called could be skipped** because the action kept its own "most enemies" target. It is now aimed at the enemy Jev chose, which the game has just confirmed as a valid target. A skipped fire writes one reason line to the log.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.1.2.6 (2026-10-29) [testing]
- **"Let Jev call the shots" now fires the PvP Limit Break.** When the Limit Break is ready, Jev is asked about this job's own Limit Break (what it does, from the game's description) with the facts that decide it: the damage against each enemy's remaining HP, Guard, Kuzushi and low-HP executes, how many enemies a line, cone or area would catch, and which allies are hurt or under attack. It fires when that wins a kill, catches several enemies, or saves the player or an ally, and holds otherwise. Only enemies the game says the Limit Break can be used on right now are offered, and the game is asked again just before firing.
- The focus pick also weighs each enemy's remaining HP and how many allies are already attacking it.
- With the setting off, or the relay slow or down, no Limit Break is fired (as before).
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.1.2.5 (2026-10-29) [testing]
- **"Let Jev call the shots"** (Targeting tab, off by default). About once a second in a PvP fight, a snapshot of jobs, HP, distance, Guard, invulnerability and crowd control (never player names) goes to a decision relay on the home network. Jev, a decision model, picks the enemy to focus; that enemy is attacked first whenever the current targeting mode allows it, after the stay-on-my-debuff-target rule.
- When the relay is slow, down or unsure, nothing changes: an answer older than three seconds is ignored and the usual targeting order applies.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.","DalamudApiLevel":15,"Description":"PvP-only auto-rotation for FFXIV. Activates in PvP zones.

    * Monk's Draconic Leap feature now properly syncs below level 50 when you don't have a form.

    1.5.0.72:
    * Double Down features now account for its new cost.

    * Added an 'Only When Full' option to Sidewinder to Pitch Perfect.

    1.5.0.70:
    * Added Comet Overwrite Prevention feature. Or did I?
    * Removed Holy overcap features (it made no sense when you gain, not lose, DPS by letting it overcap).
    
    1.5.0.69 (Nice):
    * Sacrificium Feature added.
    * Despair to Flare Star added.
    * Dragon Kick to Forbidden Chakra added.
    
    1.5.0.67:
    * Blizzard 3 & 2 to Flare Star feature added.
    
    1.5.0.61:
    * Lucid Dreaming Reminders now have a configurable MP threshold, as well as a configurable cooldown remaining offset where they stop replacing the cooldown.
    
    1.5.0.60:
    * Combos to Saber Dance during Devilment feature added.
    * Some other stuff added to Dancer, too. Maybe.
    * Phlegma to Psyche added.
    
    1.5.0.59:
    * Isle Sprint feature added.
    
    1.5.0.53:
    * Reaving Steel added from regular XIVComboExpanded. Maybe something else, too? Tis a secret.
    * Hooking Hooksets and Chummy Cast added.
    
    1.5.0.51:
    * Chaotic Glide added.
    
    1.5.0.49:
    * Standard Step into Technical Step added.
    
    1.5.0.41:
    * Viper features added.
